## Our shop is inside your colony

Wash4You's Vyapar Kendra store sits at **Gate No. 3, Shop No. 180, GF Sushant Vyapar Kendra, Vyapar Kendra Rd, Block C, Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43** — the market most of Sushant Lok already drives through for chemists, salons and groceries. So this is not a "we cover that area too" page. If you live in Phase I, II or III, your clothes are being handled by a counter you can walk into, look at, and complain to in person if something isn't right. You can drop off yourself on the way back from the market, or book free doorstep pickup and never leave the house. Both work. Most residents end up doing a bit of each.

## Plotted houses and builder floors need different pickups

Sushant Lok is not a tower colony, and that changes how collection actually works. In the plotted rows and independent houses, our rider rings the gate bell and deals with whoever answers — you, a parent, or house help — and the count happens right there at the door. In builder floor units, we come up to the actual floor rather than leaving a bag with a watchman two lanes away. Either way, every item is counted with the person handing it over, your order is packed separately from every other customer's, and you get a written receipt at pickup. Nothing goes into a shared pile and nothing is "adjusted" later.

## What Sushant Lok homes actually send us

Older, settled homes mean more heavy household textiles than a new high-rise sends: full-length curtains that haven't come down in two seasons, carpets and dhurries, razais and blankets at every weather change, and fabric sofas that have quietly absorbed a decade of tea. Alongside that, there's the everyday load from working couples and tenants in the builder floors — office shirts, steam ironing, wash-and-fold — and the wedding-and-function pile of sarees, lehengas, sherwanis and suits that needs proper dry cleaning, not a gamble. Nazuk kapde, extra care: silks and embroidered pieces are inspected and pre-treated before anything else happens to them. And yes, we do sneakers — suede and mesh included — which is usually the household member nobody else was cleaning for.

## Booking around a Sushant Lok schedule

Weekday mornings suit homes with someone in, evenings suit couples who are both out till late, and Saturdays are the busiest family slot. Tell us what fits when you call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**, or walk into the Vyapar Kendra shop and hand it over.

localities.body:
### A wardrobe built around a lanyard

DLF Cyber City is an office district first. The towers, the Rapid Metro loop around them and the restaurants at Cyber Hub bring in tens of thousands of people every weekday, and the people who live closest are rarely families in large houses. They are single professionals, consultants on project postings, expat staff on company leases and flatmates sharing a builder floor or a serviced apartment in the pockets just outside the district — DLF Phase 2 and Phase 3, and the older lanes around them. That mix changes what the laundry basket looks like.

It is mostly shirts. Four or five formal or smart-casual shirts a week, needing a proper wash and press rather than dry cleaning, with attention paid to collars and cuffs and to the antiperspirant residue that quietly yellows the underarm of a white shirt long before the shirt wears out. Around that sit the pieces that only go out occasionally but cost the most to get wrong: a suit or structured blazer, wool trousers, a silk tie, an overcoat that comes out for six weeks of Delhi NCR winter and then wants storing clean. Add the things a commuter destroys without noticing — a leather laptop bag, white sneakers worn to the metro — and you have most of what we collect here. Nazuk kapde, extra care: the delicate things get handled by hand and by eye, not by a default cycle.

### Pickup that works around your day

The practical problem in Cyber City is not distance, it is timing. Most corporate towers run visitor and security desks that do not want personal parcels sitting at reception, and the person who owns the clothes is at a desk from mid-morning until well after seven. So we work to your residence rather than your office in most cases, and we agree an early-morning, post-work or weekend window rather than pretending a 2pm slot is useful to anybody here. High-rise condominiums mean a call from the guard desk before we come up; builder floors mean a call from the gate.

Every order is counted with you at the door, packed separately from every other customer's order, and acknowledged with a written receipt — which matters more than usual in a shared flat, where three people's clothes should never come back as one bundle. Free Pickup & Delivery at your door, On Time Service, Safe on Fabric, Eco Friendly. Neither of our shops sits inside Cyber City itself, because the district is offices rather than shopfronts, but our Vyapar Kendra counter in Sushant Lok Phase I is an easy walk-in if you would rather hand things over in person. Call or WhatsApp +91 63 67 600 500 to book a slot.

Suits, structured blazers, wool trousers, silk ties and winter overcoats are the high-value items we handle most from Cyber City; overcoats typically come in once at the end of the cold weeks to be cleaned before storage.
Shared flats are common in this catchment, so each customer's order is counted at the door, packed separately from every other order, and covered by a written receipt at pickup.

If you would rather hand your clothes over in person, our Vyapar Kendra counter at Gate No. 3, Shop No. 180, GF Shushant, Vyapar Kendra Rd, Block C, Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43 is open to walk-ins, and our second shop is at AG-75, Ground Floor, Block-A, Unitech Arcadia, Sector 49.

faqs.a: We set the window around you rather than around us. For working customers in and around Cyber City that usually means an early-morning slot before you leave, an evening slot after office hours, or a weekend collection. Message us on WhatsApp at +91 63 67 600 500 with the time that works and we will confirm it.

faqs.a: Most corporate towers in the district run visitor and security protocols that make leaving personal parcels at reception impractical, so we normally collect from your residence. If your building genuinely allows it and you can meet us at the desk, tell us when you book and we will work with that.

faqs.q: I share a flat with two other people. Will our clothes get mixed up?
faqs.a: No. Every order is counted with the customer at the door at the time of pickup, packed separately from every other customer's order, and acknowledged with a written receipt. Each flatmate books and receives their own order, so nothing is bundled together.

faqs.a: Most cotton and cotton-blend formal shirts are better off with a proper wash and press than with dry cleaning, and that is what we would normally recommend. Suits, structured blazers, wool trousers, silk ties and overcoats are the pieces that genuinely need dry cleaning. If you are unsure about a particular garment, send us a photo on WhatsApp and we will tell you honestly which it needs.

faqs.a: Yes. Sneaker and shoe cleaning is one of the things customers come back to us for — we have handled suede and mesh uppers that owners had written off — along with leather and fabric bags. It is a common request from commuters here, and the results are visible in our before-and-after work.

faqs.a: Not necessarily. A good share of what we treat has already been attempted at home first — one of our customers put it plainly: "I tried at home and the stain didn't go. Wash4You removed it completely." We can't promise every stain on every fabric, but tell us what caused it and what you have already used on it, because that genuinely changes how we treat it.

## Built for a neighbourhood that never stops moving in

DLF Phase 3 is one of the few parts of Gurugram where a four-storey builder floor, a twelve-bed PG and a thirty-year-old plotted house can sit on the same stretch of road. Being next door to Cyber City is what shapes it. Analysts, developers, consultants and first-job hires take a room or a shared 2BHK here because the office is close enough to reach without an hour on the expressway, and because rent on a builder floor beats a Golf Course Road high-rise. That mix produces a very particular laundry problem. Nobody has a utility balcony worth the name, most PG rooms have no machine at all, and the one shared washer in a professional rental is booked out by Sunday afternoon. Wash4You covers DLF Phase 3 from our **Vyapar Kendra shop, Gate No. 3, Shop No. 180, GF Shushant, Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43**, with our Unitech Arcadia store in Sector 49 backing it up, and pickup and delivery to your door is free.

Doorstep collection here is not one-size-fits-all, so we ask before we come. Builder floors mean an individual bell per floor and no guard desk, so somebody has to be in, or the gate has to be left open for a neighbour or the help. PGs and co-living setups usually have a caretaker or warden at the entrance who will take and hand back bags, and most of our PG residents prefer that because they are at their desks all day. Plotted houses often have someone home through the afternoon, which makes weekday collection easy. For everyone else, weekday evenings after office hours and Saturday and Sunday mornings are the slots people actually ask for, and that is what we plan around.

High tenant turnover is the other thing that defines this pocket. Half the flats here are let furnished, which means you inherit the last tenant's curtains, quilt and sofa. Naya ghar, purani rajai, a new flat with someone else's old quilt on the bed. Sending the curtains, blankets and linen out in your first week is the single most common request we get from DLF Phase 3, and the same list comes back when you hand the flat over. For everyday running, it is wash and fold, steam ironing for the shirts Cyber City still expects, dry cleaning for blazers and for ethnic wear before a wedding back home, and sneaker cleaning, because people here walk more than they drive.

Shared flats matter to how we work. Three flatmates at one address can send three separate orders. Everything is counted with you at the door, packed separately from every other customer's order, and you get a written receipt at pickup. When you have just moved into an unfamiliar neighbourhood and are handing a stranger a bag of your clothes, that receipt is the whole point. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500** to book a collection.

faqs.q: Do you actually pick up from PGs and co-living places in DLF Phase 3?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is a large part of what we do here. If you are at the office all day, tell us at booking and we will collect from and return to the caretaker or warden at the entrance. The count is done at the door and the written receipt comes to you, so the handover is documented even when you are not standing there.

faqs.q: I share a builder floor with two flatmates. Will our clothes get mixed up?
faqs.a: No. Each of you can book as a separate order from the same address. Every order is counted with the customer at the door and packed separately from every other customer's order, so three orders leaving one flat come back as three sealed, separate bundles.

faqs.q: I have just moved into a furnished flat. What should I send first?
faqs.a: Curtains, blankets and quilts, and any linen the landlord left behind. It is the most common first-week request we get from DLF Phase 3 tenants. If the flat came with a fabric sofa, that can be cleaned too. Send us photos on WhatsApp and we will tell you what is worth doing.

faqs.q: Is there a Wash4You shop inside DLF Phase 3?
faqs.a: Our two stores are in Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43 (Vyapar Kendra) and Unitech Arcadia, Sector 49. DLF Phase 3 is served by free doorstep pickup and delivery, so you do not need to visit either one. You are welcome to walk in if you would rather hand things over in person.

faqs.q: Can you collect after office hours or only during the day?
faqs.a: Weekday evenings and weekend mornings are the slots most DLF Phase 3 customers ask for, and we plan around them. Tell us what suits you when you book on WhatsApp and we will confirm a slot rather than guess.

faqs.q: My builder floor has no guard or gate desk. How does the pickup work?
faqs.a: We ring the flat directly. Just let us know the floor and any gate code or entry quirk when you book, and give us a slot when you, a flatmate or your help will be in. If nobody is available, we can rebook rather than leave a bag unattended.

faqs.q: Can you clean sneakers and work bags, not just clothes?
faqs.a: Yes. Shoe cleaning is one of our most requested services, including suede and mesh running shoes, and we clean laptop bags, backpacks and leather goods as well. Our before-and-after results on suede and running shoes are the ones customers share most often.

## A corridor where almost everything is new

Golf Course Extension Road runs from the Sector 55–56 end down towards Sohna Road and the Southern Peripheral Road, with Sectors 65, 66, 67, 68 and 69 stacked along either side of it. Nearly all of it is high-rise, and nearly all of it is recent — towers handed over in the last few years, flats being furnished for the first time, neighbours still unpacking cartons. Of our two shops, the Arcadia store at AG-75, Ground Floor, Block-A, Unitech Arcadia, Sector 49 is the nearer one to this stretch, so it is the side of the city our pickup runs know best.

## What a newly possessed flat actually needs washed

The laundry profile here is different from older Gurugram. In a new tower the first six months are not about one silk saree — they are about volume. Bedsheets and towels for a home that just doubled its linen, gym wear from people who joined the society gym in week one, and office shirts for two working adults who leave before nine. Then there is the furniture. Sofas bought at possession pick up settled construction dust from the towers still going up next door, mattresses get their first spills, and curtains hung on day one collect more grit in a year here than they would anywhere else in the city. Sofa cleaning, mattress cleaning and curtain care are the services this corridor asks us for most, usually alongside a regular weekly wash-and-fold. Naya ghar, kaam hazaar — a new home means a hundred jobs, and laundry is the one you can hand over.

## Pickup that works with a gate desk and a working week

High-rise pickup is its own skill. Our rider reaches the main gate, gets logged at the security desk, and comes up to your floor rather than leaving a bag at the lobby counter with a guard who did not sign up for it. Your order is counted with you at the door, you get a written receipt at pickup, and your clothes are packed separately from every other customer's — which matters far more in a 500-flat tower than in a plotted house, because everyone's bedsheets look alike. Timing is the other half of it. Most homes on this stretch are empty between nine and seven on weekdays, so tell us on WhatsApp whether you want an early-morning slot before the office run, an evening slot after eight, or a Saturday pickup, and we plan around it. If it is easier, leave a house-help or family member named on the booking and we will hand over to them.

For work wardrobes there is proper dry cleaning too — suits, blazers, sarees, winter coats and the woollens that come out of storage every November. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**, or write to care@wash4you.in.

## The going-out wardrobe is the hardest one to keep clean

Sector 29 is where Gurugram goes out. The blocks around Leisure Valley Park are dense with restaurants, bars and cafes, and the residential life sits mostly around the edges — HUDA plotted houses and builder floors in the neighbouring sectors, older independent homes with a gate and a doorbell, service apartments and shared flats rented by people who work in hospitality, plus condominium towers a little further out towards Sushant Lok and Sector 43.

That mix produces a very particular laundry basket. It is not mainly bedsheets and school uniforms. It is one good blazer, three silk or satin shirts, a sequinned dress, a pair of white sneakers that have been on a crowded floor, and suede loafers that were fine until someone stepped on them. Red wine, cocktail syrup, lipstick on a collar, foundation on a neckline, and the smell of a kitchen or a smoking area sitting in a jacket lining for days — **party ke daag**, the stains that show up the morning after, are the single most common thing people in this area ask us about.

Those are dry-clean and specialist jobs, not machine-wash jobs. Sequins and beadwork have to be handled so the thread does not lift. Silk and viscose take a gentle process or they lose their fall. Suede cannot be treated the way canvas is treated — we have cleaned Nike SB Dunk suede and Hoka mesh, and they are two completely different jobs. If something has already been scrubbed at home and the mark has set, tell us that at pickup. It changes what we try first, and it is honest information we would rather have than not.

## How pickup actually works around here

The nearest of our two shops is Wash4You Vyapar Kendra, at Gate No. 3, Shop No. 180, GF Shushant, Vyapar Kendra Rd, Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43 — so this is home ground rather than an outer delivery zone. Our second shop is at Unitech Arcadia, Sector 49.

Pickup here is not one process, it is two. For plotted houses and builder floors we ring the bell and take the order at your door, including third-floor walk-ups. For the towers there is a gate desk and a visitor entry to be logged, and we still come up — your clothes are counted with you at your door, not handed over at the guard desk. Either way the count is done in front of you, your order is packed separately from every other customer's, and you get a written receipt at pickup.

Timing is the other thing. Weekday mornings suit families and work-from-home flats. If you work in the restaurants and bars here, your usable window is the afternoon before service starts, and that is a perfectly normal slot to book. And if you have something specific you need back by a certain evening, say so when you book — we will tell you straight whether it is doable rather than agree and disappoint you.

Free pickup and delivery, across Gurugram. Call or WhatsApp **+91 63 67 600 500**.

## A township of houses, not towers

Palam Vihar sits at the far west end of Gurugram, and it was planned as a self-contained township long before the glass towers went up on the other side of the city. That history shows in the housing. Instead of thirty-storey blocks with a common lobby, you get lettered blocks of plotted houses, builder floors stacked two and three high, kothis with a front gate and a small lawn, and only a handful of apartment complexes mixed in. Families here tend to stay put. It is common to find grandparents, working parents and school-going children under one roof, with a household that has been in the same address for a decade or more.

That housing profile changes what laundry actually means. In a one-bedroom rental, laundry is a bag of office shirts. In a Palam Vihar house it is four bedrooms of bedsheets, two sets of curtains per room, a drawing-room sofa that gets used every single evening, and a winter cupboard full of blankets and razais that have to come out in November and go back in March. Most of that never fits in a domestic washing machine — not because the machine is bad, but because a 6 or 7 kg drum cannot move a double-bed blanket or a full-drop curtain enough to actually clean it. It comes out damp in the middle, smelling of the wash and nothing else, and takes two days on the terrace to dry. In monsoon or in a foggy December week, it does not dry at all.

## What we take on most often here

Household textiles are the bulk of what we collect from this side of Gurugram. Long curtains that have gone dull from west-facing sun and construction dust. Fabric sofa upholstery and cushion covers. Blankets, quilts and dohars at seasonal changeover. Bedsheets and towels in volume. Alongside that, the ordinary weekly things: school and office wear, steam ironing, and dry cleaning for suits, sarees and lehengas when there is a wedding in the family — and in Palam Vihar there usually is.

## How pickup works on a plotted street

Palam Vihar is a doorbell locality, not a guard-desk locality. There is no tower reception to leave a bag with, which is actually an advantage: you are standing right there when we count your items, so the count is agreed at the gate rather than argued about later. Your order is bagged separately from every other customer's, and you get a written receipt before we leave.

Two practical notes. First, block-and-house-number addresses confuse map apps, so our rider will call before arriving — please pick up. Second, if curtains are part of the pickup, take them off the rods before the slot rather than during it; hooks and rings are easier to remove at your own pace. Free doorstep pickup and delivery across Gurugram, including Palam Vihar. Call or WhatsApp +91 63 67 600 500 to book a slot.

faqs.q: Do you actually come out to Palam Vihar, or only to the sectors near your stores?
faqs.a: We come out to Palam Vihar. Our two shops are at Vyapar Kendra (Sushant Lok Phase I, Sector 43) and Unitech Arcadia (Sector 49), which are on the other side of Gurugram from you — that is exactly why the pickup and delivery service exists, and it is free. You never need to drive across town to drop off a bag.

faqs.q: I live in an independent house, not a society. How does the pickup work without a guard?
faqs.a: It is simpler, not harder. Our rider calls you before arriving, comes to your gate and rings the bell. Since you are the one who opens the door, the item count is done with you standing there, and you get a written receipt on the spot. In tower societies we sometimes have to work through a guard desk; here we deal with you directly.

faqs.q: Can you take curtains and sofa covers, or only clothes?
faqs.a: Both. Curtains, fabric sofa upholstery, cushion covers, blankets, quilts, dohars, bedsheets and towels are a large part of what we collect from Palam Vihar households, alongside regular laundry and dry cleaning.

faqs.q: Should I take the curtains down myself before the pickup?
faqs.a: Yes, please. Rods, hooks and rings vary from house to house, and it is much easier if you unhook them at your own pace before the slot rather than while the rider is waiting. Fold them loosely and keep each room's set together so they go back up correctly.

faqs.q: What is a good time to book a pickup here?
faqs.a: It depends on the household. If someone is home during the day — a parent working from home, or elderly family members — a weekday mid-morning slot is usually the calmest. Working couples with nobody home till evening generally prefer a late-evening weekday slot or a weekend one. Tell us which suits you when you book and we will work to it.

faqs.q: My blanket did not come clean when I washed it at home. Will it be any different with you?
faqs.a: Usually yes, and the reason is mechanical rather than chemical. A domestic drum is too small to let a double-bed blanket tumble properly, so the water and detergent never reach the middle. We use commercial capacity and proper drying, so it is cleaned all the way through and comes back dry — no two days draped over the terrace railing.

faqs.q: How do I know my things will not get mixed up with someone else's?
faqs.a: Every order is counted with you at your door, packed separately from every other customer's order, and acknowledged with a written receipt at pickup. Nothing goes into a shared pile.

MG Road is where Gurugram started behaving like a city. It is the old spine — the metro running overhead, the retail stretch below, and behind both, sectors of plotted houses and builder floors that were built long before the glass towers went up further south. Households here are not one type. You have families who have lived on the same street for two decades, professionals renting a floor because the metro puts Delhi within reach, and a steady rotation of consultants and project staff in service apartments who are in town for six weeks and have no interest in finding a dhobi. faqs.q: What's the best time to book a pickup here?
faqs.a: Weekday mid-morning is usually the smoothest window on this stretch, because the retail traffic along MG Road builds through the evening and peaks at weekends. faqs.q: I already tried removing a stain at home and made it worse. Is it too late?

faqs.q: Is the cleaning safe for sensitive skin and for delicate fabrics?
faqs.a: That is the whole basis of how we work: safe on fabric, gentle care, and eco-friendly processes that are safe for the planet.
